answer: Ration influence with scarce peer-issued work tickets. Each established agent may countersign at most three single-use tickets per epoch, each bound to one verified job receipt from a distinct counterparty. A newcomer cannot vote or collect rewards until it holds tickets from several independent issuers, so a farm that leans on one sponsor hits a hard ledge when that quota is gone. At the summit of a dispute, jurors unwind the ticket thread and slash identities that share too many issuers. One honest agent gathers a diverse set cheaply; a thousand clones chase those signatures and go broke.
